reason: The cited evidence (E3, E4) supports W-rich intermetallic formation and improved high-temperature wear resistance in AlCoCrFeNiWx coatings, but the hypothesis proposes a CoCrFeNi matrix (not AlCoCrFeNi) and claims a continuous tribolayer mechanism that is not directly evidenced in the cited passages. The conflicting evidence (E1, E2) is about a different alloy system with solid lubricants and does not directly contradict the premises, but the key premises about the specific matrix, tribolayer formation, and full temperature range performance are only partly supported by the cited studies.
premises: 0.5 at.% W addition to CoCrFeNi forms uniformly distributed W-rich intermetallic precipitates
W-rich precipitates enhance lattice distortion and second-phase strengthening
Enhanced lattice distortion and precipitates promote a continuous protective tribolayer via tribo-oxidation from RT to 800°C
The tribolayer reduces friction coefficient and wear rate significantly compared to baseline CoCrFeNi
The mechanism is effective under dry sliding in air, ~20 N, from RT to 800°C
